key_insight: A measured quantum coarse-grid solution can improve fine-grid initialization for heterogeneous Darcy flow, with classical correction recovering accurate pressure fields.
engineering_relevance: The framework explores quantum-assisted finite element solvers for heterogeneous porous-media flow without placing the full fine-scale system on quantum hardware.
method: Apply a VQLS-inspired method to the Galerkin coarse system.
Reconstruct coarse solution coefficients from quantum measurements and prolongate them to the fine grid.
Initialize a classical preconditioned iterative solver with the prolonged solution.
evidence_signal: Tests on steady heterogeneous Darcy flow and a time-dependent SPE10-based problem showed improved initialization, but iteration reductions depended on the problem; all quantum computations used Qiskit Aer simulation.
watch_item: Hardware performance and net computational advantage remain unestablished, particularly when measurement and reconstruction costs are included.
paper_title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coarse-to-Fine Finite Element Solver for Heterogeneous Darcy Flow
